name: Football
rules: 11 players per side, score by getting the ball into the opponent's goal; outfield players may not use hands.
tips: Build an aerobic base first, then add short sprint intervals.
mistakes: Poor first touch under pressure; ball-watching instead of scanning the field.

name: Cricket
rules: Two teams take turns batting and bowling; the batting side scores runs, the bowling side tries to dismiss batters within their overs.
fitness: Hand-eye coordination, rotational power, short sprint speed, reaction time
tips: Throwing and catching drills build the arm strength and coordination the game demands before focusing on batting technique.
mistakes: Playing across the line of the ball; poor footwork when bowling, leading to no-balls.
equipment: Bat, ball, pads, gloves, helmet, stumps
positions: Batter, bowler, wicketkeeper, various fielding positions

name: Basketball
rules: 5 players per side, score by shooting the ball through the opponent's hoop within a shot clock.
tips: Practice footwork drills before adding shooting volume.
mistakes: Over-dribbling instead of moving the ball; poor defensive stance.
positions: Point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, center

name: Volleyball
rules: Two teams of 6 hit the ball over a net, aiming to ground it on the opponent's side within 3 touches per side.
fitness: Vertical jump, shoulder strength, agility, reaction speed
tips: Passing (the forearm dig) is the foundation skill — practice it far more than spiking early on.
mistakes: Contacting the ball with locked, straight arms during a dig; late footwork before jumping to hit.
positions: Setter, outside hitter, middle blocker, opposite, libero

name: Athletics (Track & Field)
rules: Individual timed or measured events — sprints, distance runs, jumps and throws.
tips: Technique work (start, stride) matters as much as raw fitness early on.
mistakes: Overstriding in sprints; neglecting recovery between sessions.

name: Badminton
rules: Singles or doubles, score points by landing the shuttle in the opponent's court.
tips: Shadow footwork drills build court coverage faster than hitting alone.
mistakes: Standing flat-footed between shots; weak wrist/grip control.

name: Hockey
rules: 11 players per side use sticks to hit a ball into the opponent's goal; the ball may not be touched with hands or feet.
fitness: Endurance, agility, low-stance strength, hand-eye coordination
tips: Practicing in the low athletic stance used for stick control builds the specific leg endurance the game needs.
mistakes: Standing too upright, losing close ball control; lifting the stick above shoulder height (a foul).

name: Wrestling
rules: Score points by controlling, taking down, or pinning an opponent within weight-class rules.
tips: Grip and neck strength are as important as overall body strength.
mistakes: Neglecting conditioning for match-length endurance; poor stance.

name: Boxing
rules: Two competitors score points by landing clean punches within a weight class, over a set number of rounds.
fitness: Rotational power, footwork endurance, reaction speed, core strength
tips: Footwork and defense are trained before power punching in most beginner programs — control comes first.
mistakes: Dropping hands after throwing a punch; leaning back instead of rotating out of range.

name: Swimming
rules: Individual or relay races over a fixed distance in a pool, timed to the hundredth of a second.
fitness: Cardiovascular endurance, shoulder and core strength, flexibility
tips: Stroke technique and breathing efficiency usually matter more for early progress than raw conditioning.
mistakes: Lifting the head too high to breathe, which drags the hips down and slows the stroke.
positions: Individual event or relay leg (freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly)

name: Tennis
rules: Singles or doubles, players score points by hitting the ball over the net so the opponent can't return it in play.
fitness: Agility, rotational power, endurance, reaction speed
tips: The split-step (a small hop timed to the opponent's contact) is what makes fast court coverage possible.
mistakes: Standing flat-footed at contact; using only the arm to hit instead of rotating the hips and shoulders.

name: Table Tennis
rules: Players hit a lightweight ball over a small net on a table, scoring when the opponent fails to return it legally.
fitness: Reaction speed, wrist/forearm coordination, short-range footwork
tips: Consistent, controlled rallying builds more long-term skill than swinging hard for winners early on.
mistakes: Gripping the paddle too tightly, which kills touch and control on soft shots.
